chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, and someone else, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who departed from Jam' until he arrived at Mina, and an incident occurred to him so he did not pelt the Jamarah until the sun set. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pelt twice when it is morning; one of them in the morning, and it is for the previous day, and the other at the decline of the sun, and it is for his day.'

key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: The Jamarah (the stone-pelting pillars in Mina)
key_terms.جَمْع: Jam' (the place where pilgrims gather before proceeding to Mina)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (midday, when the sun begins to move west from its zenith)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina (a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend days of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses pelting the Jamarah until sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific compensatory ritual (qada) for a pilgrim who misses the Jamarah pelting on the 11th or 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah due to an unforeseen impediment, requiring two distinct peltings the following day. Scholarly tradition emphasizes the precision of timing—morning for the missed obligation and midday for the current day—reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining the structural integrity of Hajj rites even when disrupted. This ruling underscores the balance between divine mercy for unintentional errors and the rigorous adherence to ritual order in Shia fiqh.
